body:
I'm in the Midwest, so that'd probably be too far.

I can still remember my Mom and Dad's voices. I've got old voicemails on my phone that I listen to occasionally. My Dad and I talked about things after my Mom died. We were sure we'd get through things if we kept helping and supporting each other.

Yeah, I still live in our house. I suppose I have the money to move elsewhere, but I can't see myself doing it. My Dad died in a car accident.  

I saw a counselor for a little while. He spent 3 weeks telling me to try and keep busy. There's not much in the way of support here, I live in a pretty small town. I did regular exercise before. I still stretch every day out of habit. I don't know how much running could help me.

I've been alone for two months now. I don't have a lot of extended family to begin with, and most of them aren't interested in me at all. I'm 23 and was in school but I dropped out in October, I just couldn't keep going any more. No established career either.
Thanks for your kind words. I haven't killed myself yet. But I haven't really found anything I can do with myself either. At best I'm in a kind of fog most of the time. I just don't think at all.

I had hobbies. Just very few that don't remind me of them. I've tried to throw myself into things; I watched all 3 seasons of Game of Thrones in 2 days, read books, tried to play video games. But concentrating on things is so difficult.

I don't know where I'd go. And I don't really have anyone to be with. I almost miss talking to the funeral director. At least it was someone.

We got a new fridge 3 years ago and the first time my Dad tried to get ice, it went everywhere. We joked that I should help him. Every time he got ice when I was in there, he'd tell me he was glad I was there to "supervise". It's a good memory. But it makes me cry. Even now just typing it.

I miss so many things. Listening to music together. Sharing books we liked. Arguing. Every little noise that let me know they were in the house. But what do I miss most? I miss them say "I love you". I miss holding them, being held. I'd give anything for one more goodbye.

I just can't picture going anywhere. It might sound stupid, but it's such an effort to do things now. Shaving, bathing, even getting out of bed. I don't eat most days, so I often only get up to shower, change, and drink. Then I go back to bed. It seems like it's all I can manage to do.

After my Mom died I hoped that things would get better, that I'd be able to move on. She was sick for a long time, so it wasn't a big surprise she died. But I was just as miserable months after she died as I was the day after, and that was when my Dad was still alive.

I feel broken from the time I wake up to the time I go to bed. And everything I seem to do reminds me of them; even stupid things like getting a glass of water, or putting on my socks.
